newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RECONSIDERS COMPETITION LAW - ERWIN.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RECONSIDERS COMPETITION LAW - ERWIN.

text.p: New legislation aimed at distinguishing between competition policy and monopoly law was being considered, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Wednesday.

Speaking during the debate on his 1997/98 budget, Erwin said he would ask cabinet next month to approve this approach, before it is tabled before the tri-partite National Economic and Development Council representing government, business and labour.
The government has been grappling with the competition law in South Africa's highly monopolistic economy since the African National Congress took power in 1994.
At least two drafts on the law have been dismissed.

Erwin said he would try to "draw a distinction between competition policy, which can be implemented in a wide range of legislation, and the more specific and focused that deals with monopolies and monopolistic practices."

This would support the developmental and growth goals spelt out in the macro-economic policy released last year by creating a more efficient and transparent economy with more access to economic activity.
Erwin said other legislation planned this year mainly dealt with commercial services and fair trade.

The legislation covering corporate law would be streamlined into five major pieces of legislation - the Company's Act, Securities Act, Insolvencies Act, Closed Corporations Act and a new act that would cover other ownership forms.
The Liquor Act would also be revised to take a more modern approach to the regulation of industry.
